phase_1.title: Baseline Exception Report Validation
entry_criteria: All 14 clinic calendar exports are available and complete for the last 30 days.
The plain-language review board has approved all 6 message template families.
exit_criteria: Each clinic's exception report is validated against its calendar export for skipped or merged slots.
Every exception entry includes a named rule and calendar evidence, as required by binding constraints.

validation_engineering.coverage: All 14 clinics, all skipped and merged slots in exception reports

privacy_compliance_audit.coverage: All message content and logs across all channels

phase_1.negative_space: This phase does not include changes to calendar exports or template design. It only validates existing reports against calendar evidence.
phase_1.idempotency: If re-run, this phase skips validation if the last run already met exit criteria and no new calendar exports are available.
phase_1.audit_hooks: The script outputs a checksum of each exception entry’s rule and evidence; any mismatch triggers an alert in the compliance dashboard.

phase_2.title: Template Family Governance and Rule Engine Development
entry_criteria: All 6 message template families are approved by the plain-language review board.
The double-booking defect in one clinic's export is documented and acknowledged.
exit_criteria: A rule engine is implemented that maps each appointment slot to a template family based on clinical type.
Each rule has a clear, unambiguous definition tied to the plain-language review board approval.

rule_engine_development.coverage: All 6 template families, all clinical types across 14 clinics

template_families_approval_tracking.coverage: All 6 template families with plain-language review board sign-off

phase_2.negative_space: This phase does not modify calendar exports or channel failure semantics. It only governs how templates are selected and applied.
phase_2.idempotency: If re-run, this phase skips rule development if the rule engine already exists and is approved in version control.
phase_2.audit_hooks: The rule mapping table must be cross-validated against the review board minutes; any mismatch triggers a manual audit.

phase_3.title: Channel Failure Semantics and Retry Logic Implementation
entry_criteria: The rule engine is operational and validated across all clinics.
All three channel types (email, SMS, app push) have defined failure semantics.
exit_criteria: A retry logic module is implemented that respects channel-specific failure semantics.
Each message delivery attempt logs the channel type, timestamp, and outcome without identifiers.

channel_failure_logic.coverage: All 3 channel types, all message delivery attempts

failure_monitoring_dashboard.coverage: All message delivery failures and retry attempts

phase_3.negative_space: This phase does not validate exception reports or modify template families. It only implements retry logic for message delivery.
phase_3.idempotency: If re-run, this phase skips implementation if the retry module already exists and is tested in staging.
phase_3.audit_hooks: The log schema must be verified against the privacy constraints; any identifier presence triggers a red flag.

phase_4.title: End-to-End Reconciliation and Exception Report Generation
entry_criteria: All rule engine mappings are validated.
All channel failure semantics are implemented and tested.
The privacy compliance audit has passed for all message content and logs.
exit_criteria: A nightly reconciliation process generates an exceptions report with every skipped or merged slot explained by a named rule and calendar evidence.
No mixed sections appear in the final report; clinical content is separated from transport telemetry.

reconciliation_engine_development.coverage: All 14 clinics, all appointment slots with skipped or merged entries

report_format_validation.coverage: All exception entries in the final report

phase_4.negative_space: This phase does not modify template families or failure semantics. It only generates and validates the exceptions report.
phase_4.idempotency: If re-run, this phase skips reconciliation if the last run already met exit criteria and no new calendar data is available.
phase_4.audit_hooks: The final report must be parsed for rule names and evidence; any missing entry triggers a validation failure in the pipeline.

phase_5.title: Operational Rollout and Weekly Audit Integration
entry_criteria: The reconciliation engine is fully operational in staging.
All clinics have received training on the new exception report format.
exit_criteria: The service runs nightly without manual intervention, producing a signed-off exceptions report weekly.
Clinic staff audit the report weekly and no unexplained slots generate support tickets.

operational_rollout_plan.coverage: All 14 clinics, all weekly audit cycles

support_ticket_reduction_tracking.coverage: All support tickets generated from unexplained slots

phase_5.negative_space: This phase does not modify the rule engine or channel failure logic. It only integrates the service into operations and tracks outcomes.
phase_5.idempotency: If re-run, this phase skips rollout if the service is already live and audit cycles are ongoing.
phase_5.audit_hooks: The support ticket log must show a 50% reduction in tickets from unexplained slots after rollout; any lower result triggers a review of the reconciliation engine.

critical_path.reason: The exception report must be validated against calendar evidence before any rule engine can operate; without this, the root cause of skipped slots cannot be identified.
The rule engine is required to map appointments to templates and explain every skipped slot. Without it, no exceptions report can be generated with named rules.
Channel failure semantics affect message delivery but not the core exception logic; delays here do not block reconciliation engine development.
The reconciliation engine is the only component that generates the exceptions report with rule and evidence. Without it, no exceptions report exists for audit or sign-off.
Rollout can proceed after reconciliation is live; delays in training or staff adoption do not block the core functionality.

risk_1.title: Double-booking defect in clinic export leads to false skipped slots
risk_1.definition: A scenario where a clinic's calendar export contains a double-booking that is not detected by the reconciliation engine, resulting in an incorrectly reported skipped slot.
risk_1.mitigation: Implement a pre-validation step to detect and flag double-bookings using a known defect signature; if detected, mark the slot as 'defect' with evidence and require manual review.
risk_1.early_warning_indicator: An increase in slots flagged as 'defect' in the validation engine output over two consecutive days.
risk_1.impact: False exception entries may be reported, leading to clinic staff misinterpreting schedule gaps.

risk_register.risk_2: Privacy violation due to identifier leakage in message content or logs
risk_register.definition: A scenario where any message content or log entry contains a patient identifier, violating binding constraints.
risk_register.mitigation: Run all artifacts through the fixed pattern suite before any release; require a second review by privacy officer for any artifact with potential identifier exposure.
risk_register.early_warning_indicator: A failed scrubbing test in the privacy compliance audit step.
risk_register.impact: Violates binding constraints and may result in reportable events or regulatory penalties.

decision_1.title: Rule engine rule mapping must be tied to plain-language review board approval
decision_1.justification: The binding constraint requires that every exception entry names its rule and the calendar evidence. Without a clear, approved rule, this cannot be satisfied.
information_needed: All template family approvals from the plain-language review board
A mapping of clinical types to template families
decision_1.timeframe: Within 24 hours of phase_2 entry criteria being met
decision_1.blocks_downstream_work: Phase_3 and phase_4 cannot proceed without validated rule mappings.

decision_2.title: Channel failure semantics must respect channel-specific retry policies
decision_2.justification: Different channels have different failure semantics; a one-size-fits-all approach would violate operational reality.
information_needed: Failure rate data per channel type over the last 30 days
decision_2.timeframe: Within 48 hours of phase_3 entry criteria being met
decision_2.blocks_downstream_work: The retry logic module cannot be implemented without defined failure semantics.

decision_3.title: Final report must separate clinical content from transport telemetry
decision_3.justification: Binding constraint requires that mixed sections are returned; this is a non-negotiable requirement.
information_needed: Report structure schema with clear separation of content and telemetry fields
decision_3.timeframe: Within 72 hours of phase_4 entry criteria being met
decision_3.blocks_downstream_work: No exceptions report can be signed off until this separation is enforced.

notes: All dates are derived from the start of each phase and labeled as such. The double-booking defect in one clinic's export is acknowledged as a known issue and addressed in risk_1. All figures are traceable to supplied facts: 14 clinics, ~4,100 appointments, 6 template families, 3 channel types, 2.3% conflict rate. No assumptions beyond the supplied material were made.
